story.headline: University of Washington team records a mouse embryo's cell family tree from its first division
story.summary: A team led by Jay Shendure of the University of Washington School of Medicine and Chengxiang Qiu of Dartmouth traced the lineage of a mouse embryo's cells from the fertilized egg's first division through 13.5 days of development. They inserted a recording sequence called DNA Typewriter into the egg's genome, which adds ordered genetic marks as cells divide, and reconstructed the relationships of 1.3 million cells, about 10% of the embryo, according to Nature. The results were published Oct. 8 in Science.

quote.text: Scientists have reconstructed a remarkably detailed family tree of cells in a developing mouse embryo, tracing their origins back to the moment a fertilized egg first divided into two cells.
